\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{അടിക്കുക} (aṭikkuka)}{അടിക്കുക (aṭikkuka)}]{\ml{അടിക്കുക} (aṭikkuka) — to hit, to strike}

\label{lesson:ML-C308-atikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to burst, then the Malayalam for to praise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{അടിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{അടിക്കുക}} — \emph{aṭikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to hit, to strike\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{അടിക്കുക}} (\emph{aṭikkuka}) is native Dravidian, one word with Tamil \emph{aṭu}, Kannada \emph{aḍacu} and Telugu \emph{aḍucu} (DEDR 77).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{aṭikkuka}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to burst, then the Malayalam for to praise, then say \emph{aṭikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
